conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Quantum entanglement is a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked, sharing the same fate regardless of the distance between them. When you measure the properties of one entangled particle, you instantly know the properties of its partners.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That's really interesting! So, when was this phenomenon first discovered or theorized?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: The concept of quantum entanglement was first theorized by Albert Einstein, Boris Podolsky, and Nathan Rosen in 1935. They described it in their EPR paradox paper, questioning the completeness of quantum mechanics.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Wow, that's much earlier than I would have guessed! So Einstein was involved in that too.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Indeed, Einstein famously called entanglement "spooky action at a distance" because it seemed to defy classical physics.

conversation.speaker: user_agent

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
